sso.title: Domain Authentication
sso.description: Configure SSO via HTTP header from reverse proxy (Nginx, Apache, Keycloak, ADFS)
sso.how_it_works: Domain authentication allows automatic login for users already authenticated via a corporate SSO provider. The reverse proxy passes the username in an HTTP header, and the system automatically finds or creates the account.
sso.supported_scenarios: Supported scenarios: Nginx + Kerberos, Apache + mod_auth_kerb, Keycloak proxy, ADFS + WAP, Traefik + ForwardAuth.
sso.status_off_desc: Local administrators can still sign in. Configure the header and test normalization before enabling domain authentication.
sso.status_ready_desc: Incoming users are resolved from the configured HTTP header. Keep at least one local admin account available as a fallback.
sso.status_error_desc: Set the HTTP header before enabling SSO, otherwise the backend cannot identify the authenticated user.
sso.enable_desc: Auto-login via HTTP header from reverse proxy
sso.http_header_hint: HTTP header name containing the username. Common values: REMOTE_USER, X-Forwarded-User, X-Remote-User
sso.test_header_hint: Paste an example value from your proxy to preview the username WebTerm will use.
sso.test_missing_header: Enter the HTTP header name first.
sso.test_missing_value: Enter a sample username from the proxy header.
sso.default_profile_hint: Which access profile to assign to users auto-created via SSO
sso.auto_create_desc: If user is not found in DB, create account automatically
